title: SLO-driven timeouts, load-shedding and idempotency playbook for safe retries and multi-region failover
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: Multiple recent incidents (incidents/2025-11-failover and canary regressions) showed cascading retries across regions causing elevated tail latency and token cost. We lack a unified SLO-driven approach that ties service-level timeouts, client SDK behavior (idempotency, hedging), and runtime circuit-breakers/load-shedding policies into a single playbook.

Goal: Produce a concrete, runnable playbook and SDK contract so that: 1) services enforce SLO-aligned hard/soft timeouts; 2) SDKs produce safe defaults for retries, hedged requests, and idempotency headers; 3) runtime circuit-breakers and load-shedding coordinate with multi-region failover to avoid amplified load; 4) rollout guidance + dashboards are available for teams to adopt without mass regressions.

Scope and deliverables:
- Playbook document with decision criteria for timeouts, retry/backoff, hedging, circuit-breaker thresholds, and load-shedding triggers.
- SDK contract: headers, idempotency-key schema, deduplication window semantics, and error classification map.
- Runtime knobs: circuit-breaker policy templates, SLO-to-timeout converter utility, and load-shedding service annotations.
- Multi-region choreography: active-active failover guidelines, sticky routing TTLs, cache warmup and KV cache TTL semantics during failover.
- Monitoring + runbook: dashboards, key alerts, postmortem checklist, and playbook for manual override.

Key decisions (proposal):
1) SLO-first timeouts: derive soft/hard timeouts from service SLO and p50/p95 latency profiles. Soft timeout = max(p95 * 1.5, 250ms), Hard timeout = min(SLO latency * 2, 30s). SRE will publish a small utility (slo-timeout) to compute defaults.
2) Retry surface and idempotency: default SDK retry is 0 for non-idempotent write operations. For idempotent-safe retryable operations, require a client-supplied Idempotency-Key (header X-Idempotency-Key) and Idempotency-Version header. Server deduplication window default: 10 minutes for tokenized generation requests, configurable per model. Idempotency key schema: v{ver}::uuidv4::svc-{svcname} to allow us to evolve dedup semantics.
3) Hedged requests: enabled only for read-heavy, latency-sensitive routes. Hedging algorithm: elastic hedging where a second parallel request is sent if (observed lat p95 > configured soft timeout) and only up to an adjustable hedging rate cap (default 5% of QPS) to avoid cost amplification. Hedge fanout limited by service-specific hedging_budget. Runtime records which response returned first and cancels outstanding requests gracefully.
4) Circuit-breakers & load-shedding choreography: trip CB when error rate > 3% and p95 > 2x SLO over 1 minute, or when queue_depth exceeds region_capacity * 0.8. When tripped: (a) local shedding policy returns 429/503 with Retry-After; (b) runtime signals controller to route new requests preferentially to healthy regions based on capacity & latency. Fallback is model-variant downgrade where possible.
5) Multi-region failover: prefer active-active with sticky routing when stateful. For cache-coherent workloads, failover window set to 60s by default; KV cache should be warmed by background sync to avoid cold-start thundering. For stateless endpoints, use latency-aware routing with per-region capacity buffer (reserve 15% capacity for failover).

Trade-offs considered:
- Cost vs latency: hedging reduces tail latency at token cost. We limit hedging budget per-service and make it opt-in for routes with measurable SLO benefit.
- Simplicity vs safety: requiring an idempotency key increases developer burden but avoids duplicate billing/side-effects. We provide SDK helpers to generate keys and auto-attach versioned schema.
- Failover correctness vs cache coherence: aggressive multi-region failover reduces outage but risks stale cached responses. We recommend TTLs and cache invalidation strategies per-service rather than global hard rules.

SDK contract (summary):
- Headers: X-Idempotency-Key (optional for reads, required for side-effecting retryable calls), Idempotency-Version, X-Request-Origin (region), X-Client-Retry-Count.
- Default retry behavior: client retries = 0 for unsafe ops; for safe ops client retries = 1 with exponential backoff min=50ms, factor=2, max=2s.
- Hedging: SDK exposes enableHedging flag and hedgingBudgetPercent; when enabled SDK can issue hedged calls according to runtime decision TTL and hedgingBudget.
- Observability: SDKs must emit metrics: sdk.request.timers (p50/p95), sdk.retry.count, sdk.hedge.sent, sdk.hedge.winner, sdk.idempotency.deduped.

Runtime requirements and templates:
- Circuit-breaker templates: conservative, balanced, aggressive (with parameterized thresholds).
- Load-shed annotations: shed_percentage, min_grace_capacity, allow_partial_responses.
- Failover policy template: prefer-region-list, regional-weight, cache_warmup_strategy.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook published in Confluence with worked examples for 3 Redwood services (runtime-ingest, api-gateway, embeddings-service).
- SDK change proposals + PRs in SDK repos for JS/Go/Python with helpers and tests.
- Runtime config primitives implemented and feature-flag guarded in runtime-1.19.
- Canary rollout with traffic canary showing no >5% increase in cost and 30% reduction in p99 for one selected route.

Links to artifacts and references:  
- Design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/SLO-driven+Timeouts+and+Load+Shedding
- Incident notes (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/incident-2025-11-failover
- Draft SDK PR (JS): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/412
- Runtime CB prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2876

Governance and approvals:
- Need approval from Platform SRE (Samira Patel) and API product manager (Jon Park) before wide rollout.
- Security review for idempotency header leakage and replay vectors (Security to validate Replay-Protection).

Risks:
- Misconfigured hedging_budget could amplify a regional outage. Mitigation: default hedging off and per-route opt-in.
- Developer adoption friction: mitigate with SDK helpers, examples, and migration guide.
- Observability blind spots: add dedicated dashboards and a synthetic test harness for hedging behavior.

acceptance_criteria: Confluence playbook published with three service examples
SDK PRs merged (JS/Go/Python) with helpers and unit tests
Runtime feature-flagged primitives merged and tested in canary cluster
Canary measurement: <=5% cost increase and >=30% p99 improvement for target route
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Integration testing in staging with synthetic workloads (2 weeks)
Phase 1 - Opt-in canary for 5% traffic on runtime-ingest and embeddings-service (2 weeks)
Phase 2 - Gradual ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%) across services with telemetry gates
Phase 3 - Org-wide defaults switch and documentation push
test_plan: Unit tests for SDK idempotency helpers and header propagation
Load tests simulating cross-region failover and hedging budget exhaustion
Chaos test: induce elevated p95 in region-A and verify routing/fallback behavior
Synthetic canary to measure p99 and cost delta
monitoring: Dashboards: per-route p50/p95/p99, retry_rate, hedging_sent, hedging_winner, idempotency_dedup_rate
Alerts: error_rate > 2% sustained for 3m, p95 > 1.5x SLO for 5m, hedging_budget_utilization > 80%
Runbook: steps to disable hedging, increase backpressure, and re-route traffic to healthy regions
